integrator_questions: Did line_loss_events fall on the oval, s-bend and slalom with the array at y = 0.075 m? Where does the first loss occur on each track?
Does max_error drop below 0.06 m, or does the robot still leave the track at the same bend?
Does steering_oscillation keep rising with the forward array, and does kd still damp the signal?
If line loss is 0 but the robot still leaves the track, is the limit wheel-command saturation (+/-4095) or control response?
Do any runs finish, and what is completion_time? Is there speed margin to raise base_speed toward 1.5 m/s average?

intent: Kept the 50 mm span and every other geometry value from iteration 3, and moved only the array forward from y = 0.065 m to y = 0.075 m. This follows the Integrator's rule, since line loss was still 1.7 to 2.0 events per track at y = 0.065 m. I expect line_loss_events to fall on the oval and s-bend, progress to rise above the iteration-3 values (0.27, 0.21, 0.14), and the score to beat 82.8. I am considering, without committing yet, narrowing wheel_track to about 0.10 m for more turn rate, but only if line loss reaches 0 and max_error stays at or above 0.06. I am not changing mass or body width, because neither is shown to limit the outcome.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) the remaining line loss comes from insufficient reaction distance on bend entries, so moving the array to y = 0.075 m should reduce it; (2) once line loss is 0, the binding limit is turning authority, which a narrower wheel_track should relieve; (3) the forward array's added jitter is not large enough to offset its benefit, since steering_oscillation has stayed at 0.2 to 0.24. Measurements requested per track: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort. line_loss_events separates sensor coverage from control, and max_error shows whether drift still reaches the off-track limit.
rationale: Iteration 3 moved the array from y = 0.055 m to y = 0.065 m with the 50 mm span. Score rose from 65.3 to 82.8, and progress improved on every track (oval 0.22 to 0.27, s-bend 0.15 to 0.21, slalom 0.11 to 0.14). Line loss did not clear, though: 2.0 events on the oval, 2.0 on the s-bend and 1.7 on the slalom. max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.066, still above the 0.06 m off-track floor. Steering oscillation rose modestly to 0.20 to 0.24, so the forward array is adding some jitter but not destabilising the loop. The Integrator's rule for this case is that if line_loss_events is still at least 1 on any development track at y = 0.065 m, move the array to about y = 0.075 m and keep the 50 mm span. Line loss is still at least 1 on all three tracks, so I follow that rule and set y = 0.075 m, which is inside the 0.08 m limit. I keep the span, five sensors, the 12 mm footprint, the 0.12 m track, the 0.03 m wheels, the 0.6 kg mass and the 0.12 m body width. The Integrator's wheel_track change only applies once line loss reaches 0 and max_error stays at or above 0.06, so it is not yet triggered. Widening the body does not change the off-track limit, which is already at its 0.06 m floor. I took the Integrator's advice. Expected result: line_loss_events falls on the oval and s-bend, progress rises further, and the score improves on 82.8. Risk: the s-bend loss count rose from 1 to 2 when the array moved forward, so the sensors may be losing the tape on tight entries. steering_oscillation is the watch point.
